gap_candidates.description: History receives everything chronologically | Multiple Orchestrator runs within the same project may be completely unrelated | Priority-1 docs requiring canon cleanup: Plans/Orchestrator_Page.md, Plans/Executor_Protocol.md, Plans/Contracts_V0.md, Plans/storage-plan.md, Plans/human-in-the-loop.md | Progress: summarized active concerns | Revocation and reopen labels must be: Promotion Revoked, Seam Completion Revoked, Reopened, Reopened by Patch, Reopened by New Evidence
exact_missing_items: chat/thread only for genuine user decision/input
system notifications reserved for high-value sparse events
Multiple Orchestrator runs within the same project may be completely unrelated
historical run must not imply: predecessor/successor relationship, continuation of the same orchestration thread, supersession by a newer project run, shared seam/package/node identity
same project does not mean related; same repo does not mean related; temporal order does not mean related
Priority-1 docs requiring canon cleanup: Plans/Orchestrator_Page.md, Plans/Executor_Protocol.md, Plans/Contracts_V0.md, Plans/storage-plan.md, Plans/human-in-the-loop.md
Ledger: exact concern record, sources, lineage, merge/split/supersession, acknowledgment/dismissal rationale
Search should support: active concerns, acknowledged concerns, dismissed concerns, concern lineage lookups by prior id
Revocation and reopen labels must be: Promotion Revoked, Seam Completion Revoked, Reopened, Reopened by Patch, Reopened by New Evidence
Seam-level acceptance dimensions (5): operability, state coherence, workflow completeness, UX coherence, architectural coherence

Seam-level failure classes (10, formalized): GUI/runtime mismatch, incomplete end-to-end flow, cross-package state mismatch, contract drift, technically-wired-but-operationally-unusable, local-pass/global-fail composition, missing degraded/recovery behavior, inconsistent UX semantics, cross-seam architecture drift, invisible governance/missing operator affordances
Treat quiet or temporary suppression as UI-notification behavior, not concern dismissal
Treat acknowledged as escalation/noise control and ownership visibility, not semantic closure and not blocker removal by itself
